about: Hand-check sample: 20 apps drawn at random (2 per category, random.Random(2026)). Each was labeled from the live official docs by an independent verifier that never saw the pipeline output, then spot-checked in a browser. Labels follow data/rubric.md.

apps.name: HubSpot

auth: Any app designed for installation by multiple HubSpot accounts ... must use OAuth.
access: Developer test accounts are free HubSpot accounts
official_mcp: HubSpot offers two distinct MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers

apps.notes: api_key = private app access token (legacy private-app creation ends Oct 2026).

apps.name: Podio

auth: The Podio API uses the OAuth2 protocol for authentication.
access: It's easy to get one or more API keys for accessing your Podio data.
official_mcp: no MCP repository in the vendor org

apps.notes: api_key = app ID + app token (app-auth grant).

apps.name: Gorgias

auth: Since we're using HTTP Basic Authentication, the USERNAME:API_KEY pair has to be a base64 encoded string.
access: You don't need to follow any special process to create a private app.
official_mcp: The Gorgias MCP is a first-party connector

apps.notes: Public (multi-tenant) apps need OAuth2 + Developer Portal review.

apps.name: Gladly

auth: Gladly API uses token-based Basic Authentication.
access: First, you'll need to set up an account with the necessary API permissions.
official_mcp: Gladly needs to have turned on the Gladly MCP for your organization.

apps.notes: No self-serve signup; the API needs an existing Gladly org (sales-led).

apps.name: Twilio

auth: use HTTP Basic authentication. Use your API key SID as the username
access: You can sign up for a Twilio free trial account without a credit card.
official_mcp: The Twilio Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives AI coding agents direct, structured access

apps.notes: other = JWT access tokens for client SDKs.

apps.name: Lark (Larksuite)

auth: Obtain the App ID and App Secret, which will be used for API authentication
access: Click 'Console' and create a new application
official_mcp: This is the Feishu/Lark official OpenAPI MCP

apps.notes: open.larksuite.com docs are JS-rendered; evidence from the vendor GitHub org.

apps.name: Threads (Meta)

auth: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
access: To access the Threads API, create an app and pick the Threads use case.
official_mcp: Connect your Threads account to an AI assistant with the Threads MCP server

apps.notes: Self-serve for own/tester accounts; App Review before serving the public.

auth: To use an API key, include an Authorization header with the value Bearer
access: Sign up for our free plan (no credit card required)
official_mcp: no MCP repository in the vendor org

apps.name: Ecwid

access: Only stores on paid plans can access API.
official_mcp: no MCP repository in the vendor org

apps.notes: Developers can request a free paid-plan upgrade by email (not self-serve).

apps.name: Amazon Selling Partner

auth: Standard OAuth 2.0 redirect-based flow for web applications
official_mcp: A local MCP server that bundles SP-API developer tools

apps.notes: Needs a Seller/Vendor Central developer registration that Amazon approves.

apps.name: Sherlock

auth: To search for only one user: sherlock user123

apps.notes: Local CLI only; wrapping it means hosting it yourself.

apps.name: Clay

access: Enterprise (custom pricing with annual commitment) ... Clay API access
official_mcp: Clay MCP for Reps | Search, enrich, and reach out to leads from your AI chat tool | Included

apps.notes: Browser-checked. Full Clay API is Enterprise-only (sales-led); free plan gets a capped CLI/API search quota and the MCP. No public API reference, so auth/api_type are not scored.

apps.name: GitHub

auth: you can create a personal access token
access: If you want to use the GitHub REST API for personal use, you can create a personal access token.

apps.notes: GitHub also has a public GraphQL API (docs.github.com/graphql), so api_type=both. other = GitHub App JWT.

auth: Create an API token to grant access to the API
access: go to My Profile > API Tokens
official_mcp: the recommended Cloudflare API MCP Server is maintained in cloudflare/mcp

auth: We currently support using personal access tokens and OAuth access tokens
access: The personal access tokens panel can be accessed at /create/tokens.

apps.name: Harvest

auth: Implementing a full OAuth2 Authentication flow
access: creating a Personal Access Token from the Developers section of Harvest ID

apps.notes: Free trial account is enough to mint a token.

apps.name: Plaid

auth: /oauth/token ... conform to the OAuth 2.0 specification. client_credentials allows exchanging a client id and client secret
access: To gain access to the Plaid API, create an account on the Plaid Dashboard.
official_mcp: Plaid offers two Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers: The Dashboard MCP server is a remote MCP server hosted by Plaid.

apps.notes: Sandbox is self-serve; production access is requested through the Dashboard. Gold corrected after the agent surfaced the OAuth and MCP pages (browser-confirmed).

apps.name: iPayX

auth: Every request requires a Bearer token in the Authorization header.
access: Upgrade to the 100-audit Credit Pack or Unlimited for API access
official_mcp: Connect your AI agent to real-time FX audit verdicts.

apps.notes: Docs conflict: MCP page mentions a free 10-audits/day key; homepage says upgrade for API access.

apps.name: Otter AI

access: Yes, Otter offers a public API for Enterprise customers. To get started, contact your Otter account manager

apps.notes: Browser-checked (help.otter.ai blocks scripted fetches). REST API is Enterprise-only via account manager, but the official MCP is OAuth for any Otter user.

auth: This is a command-line interface (CLI) for mermaid.
access: It takes a mermaid definition file as input and generates an SVG/PNG/PDF file

corrections.name: Plaid
corrections.why: The independent verifier marked Plaid MCP 'unconfirmed' and missed the OAuth token service. The agent cited plaid.com/docs/resources/mcp and plaid.com/docs/api/oauth; both confirmed by hand in a browser.
